Dear Sir/Madam, 
 
This is with reference to the communications received from the Stock Exchanges seeking clarification on the 
news report dated 30 October 2026 captioned “India orders Sun Pharma to halt eye-care drug production at 
plant after quality lapses” (“News Report”) and the movement in the price of the Company’s shares. 
  
In this regard, Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited (“Company”) submits as follows: 
  
The News Report relates to developments that occurred in August 2026 and does not concern any new event or 
development occurring on 30 October 2026. The matter was assessed at the relevant time and was not considered 
to warrant a disclosure under Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations. 
 
As regards the share price movement, it may also be noted that the Company announced its financial results for 
the quarter and half year ended 30 September 2026 on 30 October 2026. The Company is not in a position to 
attribute the movement in its share price to the News Report or to any particular factor. 
 
The Company further confirms that it is not aware of any material event or information requiring disclosure 
under Regulation 30 that has not been disclosed to the Stock Exchanges and that could explain the aforesaid 
movement in the price of its shares. 
 
Thank you. 
 
For Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited 
 
 
 
(Anoop Deshpande) 
Company Secretary and Compliance Officer

U.S. 
U.S. sales for Q2 FY2027 were INR 30,202 Mn up 9.3% compared to INR 27,624 Mn in Q2 FY2026; (USD 317 Mn  
in Q2 FY2027 compared with USD 314 Mn in Q2 FY2026); accounting for 39% of Lupin’s global sales. 
 
 
The Company received 4 ANDA and 1 NDA 505(b)(2) approvals from the U.S. FDA, and launched 1 product in the 
quarter in the U.S. The Company now has 149 generic products in the U.S. Market. 
 
Lupin continues to be the 3rd largest pharmaceutical player in both U.S. generic market and U.S. total market by 
prescriptions (IQVIA Quarter September 2026). Lupin is the leader in 61 of its marketed generics in the U.S. and 
amongst the Top 3 in 113 of its marketed products (IQVIA Quarter September 2026 by extended units). 
 
India  
India sales for Q2 FY2027 were INR 23,836 Mn, up 14.7% compared to INR 20,777 Mn in Q2 FY2026; accounting 
for 31% of Lupin’s global sales. India Region Formulation sales up by 13.8% in the quarter as compared to Q2 
FY2026.  
 
The Company launched 5 brands across therapies during the quarter. Lupin is the 8th largest company in the Indian 
Pharmaceutical Market (IQVIA MAT September 2026). 
 
Other Developed Markets 
Other Developed markets sales for Q2 FY2027 were INR 11,823 Mn, up 45.7% compared to INR 8,117 Mn in Q2 
FY2026; accounting for 15% of Lupin’s global sales. 
 
Emerging Markets  
 
Emerging Markets sales for Q2 FY2027 were INR 8,908 Mn, down 3.5% compared to INR 9,228 Mn in Q2 FY2026; 
accounting for 11% of Lupin’s global sales. 
 
Global API 
Global API sales for Q2 FY2027 were INR 3,086 Mn, up 20.2% compared to INR 2,568 Mn in Q2 FY2026; accounting 
for 4% of Lupin’s global sales. 
 
Research and Development 
Investment in R&D was INR 6,181 Mn (7.9% of sales) for the quarter as compared to INR 5,222 Mn (7.6% of sales) 
for Q2 FY2026. 
 
Lupin received approval for 4 ANDA and 1 NDA 505(b)(2) from the U.S. FDA in the quarter. Cumulative ANDA filings 
with the U.S. FDA stand at 429 as of September 30, 2026, with the company having received 353 approvals to date. 
 
The Company now has 48 First-to-File (FTF) filings including 21 exclusive FTF opportunities. Cumulative U.S. DMF 
filings stand at 94 as of September 30, 2026.

About Lupin 
 
Lupin Limited is a global pharmaceutical leader headquartered in Mumbai, India, with products distributed in over 
100 markets. Lupin specializes in pharmaceutical products, including branded and generic formulations, complex 
generics, biotechnology products, and active pharmaceutical ingredients. Trusted by healthcare professionals and 
consumers globally, the company enjoys a strong position in India and the U.S. across multiple therapy areas, 
including respiratory, cardiovascular, anti-diabetic, anti-infective, gastrointestinal, central nervous system, and 
women’s health. Lupin has 15 state-of-the-art manufacturing sites and 6 research centers globally, along with a 
dedicated workforce of over 26,000 professionals. Lupin is committed to improving patient health outcomes 
through its subsidiaries – Lupin Diagnostics, Lupin Digital Health, and Lupin Manufacturing Solutions. 
  
To know more, visit www.lupin.com or follow us on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/lupin

U.S. sales for Q2 FY2027 were INR 30,202 Mn up 9.3% compared to INR 27,624 Mn in Q2 FY2026; (USD 317 Mn  
in Q2 FY2027 compared with USD 314 Mn in Q2 FY2026); accounting for 39% of Lupin’s global sales. 
 
 
The Company received 4 ANDA and 1 NDA 505(b)(2) approvals from the U.S. FDA, and launched 1 product in the 
quarter in the U.S. The Company now has 149 generic products in the U.S. Market. 
 
Lupin continues to be the 3rd largest pharmaceutical player in both U.S. generic market and U.S. total market by 
prescriptions (IQVIA Quarter September 2026). Lupin is the leader in 61 of its marketed generics in the U.S. and 
amongst the Top 3 in 113 of its marketed products (IQVIA Quarter September 2026 by extended units). 
 
India

for 31% of Lupin’s global sales. India Region Formulation sales up by 13.8% in the quarter as compared to Q2 
FY2026.  
 
The Company launched 5 brands across therapies during the quarter. Lupin is the 8th largest company in the Indian 
Pharmaceutical Market (IQVIA MAT September 2026). 
 
Other Developed Markets 
Other Developed markets sales for Q2 FY2027 were INR 11,823 Mn, up 45.7% compared to INR 8,117 Mn in Q2 
FY2026; accounting for 15% of Lupin’s global sales. 
 
Emerging Markets  
 
Emerging Markets sales for Q2 FY2027 were INR 8,908 Mn, down 3.5% compared to INR 9,228 Mn in Q2 FY2026; 
accounting for 11% of Lupin’s global sales. 
 
Global API 
Global API sales for Q2 FY2027 were INR 3,086 Mn, up 20.2% compared to INR 2,568 Mn in Q2 FY2026; accounting 
for 4% of Lupin’s global sales. 
 
Research and Development

for Q2 FY2026.

with the U.S. FDA stand at 429 as of September 30, 2026, with the company having received 353 approvals to date.

The Company and its subsidiary are exposed to multiple civil lawsuits alleging anticompetitive behavior related to certain products and a
possible violation of federal and state antitrust laws.These lawsuits were combined into the collection of similar cases referred to as In
Re Generic Pharmaceuticals Antitrust Litigation. Such litigation are often resolved through settlement agreements. During the year
ended March 31 2026, the Company on best estimate recorded a provision of ₹ 4,493.9 million (USD 50.0 million) towards this litigation
without admission of liability or wrongdoing. During the quarter ended March 31, 2026, this provision has been recorded by the
subsidiary and consequently reversed in the standalone results. During the period ended September 30, 2026, the wholly owned
subsidiary settled one of the ongoing antitrust matters for an amount of ₹ 3,162.8 million (USD 35.8 million) without admission of liability
or wrongdoing.
On February 09, 2026, Lupin Limited and its subsidiary entered into a settlement agreement with Astellas towards ongoing dispute
related to Mirabegron ER Tablets a generic version of Myrbetriq ER Tablets in US markets and agreed to pay USD 90.0 million. During
the year ended March 31, 2026, the Company has compensated Lupin Pharmaceuticals, Inc., U.S.A., for the settlement payment of ₹
1,364.7 million (USD 15.0 million) made by it and accordingly expensed. The balance amount of USD 75.0 million towards prepaid
option has been paid and capitalised by the subsidiary.
The Government of India has consolidated 29 existing labour legislations into a unified framework comprising four labour codes as
follows: Code on Wages, 2019, Code on Social Security, 2020, Industrial Relations Code, 2020 and Occupational Safety, Health and
Working Conditions Code, 2020 (collectively referred to as the "New Labour Codes"). The New Labour Codes are effective from
November 21, 2025 and introduce changes that include, among other things, setting a uniform definition of wages. The Company has
assessed the implications of the New Labour Codes and has recognized an incremental cost of ₹ 496.4 million during the year ended
March 31, 2026.
During the previous periods ended September 30, 2025 and March 31, 2026, the Company transferred its Over the Counter ('OTC') and
API R&D business in India to its wholly owned subsidiaries Lupinlife Consumer Healthcare Limited and Lupin Manufacturing Solutions
Limited respectively, as a going concern on slump sale basis for a consideration of ₹ 8,200.0 million and ₹ 180.0 million resulting in gain
on divestment of ₹ 6,589.6 million and ₹ 37.2 million respectively.

deferred tax liability ₹ 309.8 million, Goodwill ₹ 325.9 million has been accounted based on report of independent valuer.

The Company and its subsidiary are exposed to multiple civil lawsuits alleging anticompetitive behavior related to certain products and a
possible violation of federal and state antitrust laws.These lawsuits were combined into the collection of similar cases referred to as In
Re Generic Pharmaceuticals Antitrust Litigation. Such litigation are often resolved through settlement agreements. During the year
ended March 31 2026, the Company on best estimate recorded a provision of ₹ 4,493.9 million (USD 50.0 million) towards this litigation
without admission of liability or wrongdoing. During the quarter ended March 31, 2026, this provision has been recorded by the
subsidiary and consequently reversed in the standalone results. During the period ended September 30, 2026, the wholly owned
subsidiary settled one of the ongoing antitrust matters for an amount of ₹ 3,162.8 million (USD 35.8 million) without admission of liability
or wrongdoing.
On February 09, 2026, Lupin Limited and its subsidiary entered into a settlement agreement with Astellas towards ongoing dispute
related to Mirabegron ER Tablets a generic version of Myrbetriq ER Tablets in US markets and agreed to pay USD 90.0 million. During
the year ended March 31, 2026, the Company has compensated Lupin Pharmaceuticals, Inc., U.S.A., for the settlement payment of ₹
1,364.7 million (USD 15.0 million) made by it and accordingly expensed. The balance amount of USD 75.0 million towards prepaid
option has been paid and capitalised by the subsidiary.
The Government of India has consolidated 29 existing labour legislations into a unified framework comprising four labour codes as
follows: Code on Wages, 2019, Code on Social Security, 2020, Industrial Relations Code, 2020 and Occupational Safety, Health and
Working Conditions Code, 2020 (collectively referred to as the "New Labour Codes"). The New Labour Codes are effective from
November 21, 2025 and introduce changes that include, among other things, setting a uniform definition of wages. The Company has
assessed the implications of the New Labour Codes and has recognized an incremental cost of ₹ 496.4 million during the year ended
March 31, 2026.
During the previous periods ended September 30, 2025 and March 31, 2026, the Company transferred its Over the Counter ('OTC') and
API R&D business in India to its wholly owned subsidiaries Lupinlife Consumer Healthcare Limited and Lupin Manufacturing Solutions
Limited respectively, as a going concern on slump sale basis for a consideration of ₹ 8,200.0 million and ₹ 180.0 million resulting in gain
on divestment of ₹ 6,589.6 million and ₹ 37.2 million respectively.

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE 
 
Equitas Small Finance Bank Limited announces Mr. Balaji Nuthalapadi as Interim CEO, subject to 
RBI Approval 
 
Board initiates the process to identify a successor to Mr. P. N. Vasudevan 
 
India, November 4, 2026: Equitas Small Finance Bank Limited announced on 3 November 2026 that 
its Board of Directors, based on the recommendation of the Nomination and Remuneration 
Committee, has approved the appointment of Mr. Balaji Nuthalapadi, currently serving as a Whole-
Time Director (Executive Director) of the Bank, as its Interim Chief Executive Officer (CEO), subject 
to the approval of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).  
 
As Executive Director at Equitas Small Finance Bank Limited, Mr. Balaji Nuthalapadi has played a 
pivotal role in enhancing digital capabilities, upgrading technology and improving operational 
efficiency. Prior to joining Equitas Small Finance Bank Limited, he was with Citi for 28 years and 
served as Managing Director and Head of India Citi Solutions Centers and Head of India Operations 
and Technology. He worked in multiple geographies across Asia & EMEA in roles spanning asset 
sales, wealth management, re-engineering, consumer operations and technology and Global 
Capability Center leadership where he led the scale-up of Citi’s global hubs in India. 
 
The appointment follows the resignation of Mr. P. N. Vasudevan as Managing Director and CEO of 
the Bank. Mr. Balaji Nuthalapadi's appointment will take effect from the date of RBI approval or such 
other date as may be stipulated by the RBI. Equitas Small Finance Bank Limited shall ensure to its 
stakeholders and investors that smooth and seamless transition which connote stability. 
 
The Board has placed on record its deep appreciation and sincere gratitude to Mr. P. N. Vasudevan 
for his invaluable contributions, exemplary leadership and dedicated service to the Bank during his 
tenure. The Bank will determine his relieving date following the receipt of RBI approval for the interim 
CEO appointment and in consultation with Mr. P. N. Vasudevan. 
 
The Board has also initiated the process of identifying a successor to Mr. P. N. Vasudevan and will 
submit its recommendation to the RBI in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements. 
 
Equitas Small Finance Bank Limited remains committed to its strategic priorities, business objectives 
and its mission of delivering inclusive, responsible and customer-centric banking services. The Bank 
will continue to focus on strengthening its customer relationships, expanding its reach and creating 
sustainable value for all its stakeholders. 
 
About Equitas Small Finance Bank Limited (ESFB) 
Equitas Small Finance Bank Limited is one of the largest small finance banks in India. As a new-age 
bank, we offer a bouquet of products and services tailored to meet the needs of our customers – 
individuals with limited access to formal financing channels, as well as affluent and mass affluent, 
Small & Medium Enterprises (SMEs) and corporates. Our firmly entrenched strategy focuses on 
providing credit to the unbanked and underbanked micro and small entrepreneurs, developing 
products to address the growing aspirations at the ‘bottom of the pyramid’, fuelled by granular 
deposits and ‘value for money’ banking relationships.

Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to Q2 and H1 FY27 LT Foods 
Earnings Call. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode 
and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation 
concludes. Should you need assistance during the conference call, please signal 
an operator by pressing star then zero on your touchtone phone. Please note

Sumant Kumar from Motilal Oswal. Thank you and over to you, sir. 
Sumant Kumar: 
Thank you. Good evening, everyone and a very warm welcome to LT Foods to 
Q2FY27 Post Result Earnings Call hosted by Motilal Oswal Financial Services. On 
the call today, we have management team being represented by Mr. Ashwani 
Kumar Arora, MD and CEO, Mr. Sachin Gupta, CFO and Ms. Monika Chawla 
Jaggia, Chief Corporate Development Officer. We will begin the call with the key 
thoughts from the management team. Thereafter, we will open the floor for 
the Q&A session. I would now like to request the management to share their 
perspective on the performance of the company. Thank you and over to you. 
Monika Chawla: 
Thank you, Sumant, for the introduction. Along with us, we have Mr. Ritesh 
Arora as well. He is the CEO of India and Far East business. So, good evening, 
everyone and thank you for joining us today on the post Q2 and H1FY27 
earnings conference call of LT Foods Limited.  
Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made 
during this call may constitute forward-looking statements. These statements 
are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and 
uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those 
expressed or implied.  
The result documents are available on our company's website as well as the 
stock exchanges. So, I'll start with a brief strategic update across our key 
geographies and businesses. Across markets, our priorities remain consistent, 
strengthen our brands, expand consumer reach, build differentiated portfolio, 
deepen distribution and invest in capabilities that support sustainable and 
profitable growth.  
I'll start with India. India continues to be a strong growth engine for LT Foods. 

LT Foods Limited 
October 28, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 22 
 
Our strategy is centered on premiumization, portfolio expansion, deeper 
distribution and digitally enabled execution. During the quarter, we 
strengthened our portfolio with Daawat Delight, Rozana Platinum, and new 
formats such as biryani gravy and biryani masala.  
We are also seeing encouraging traction in health-focused offerings, including 
brown, red and black rice, while our biryani kits have grown by 38% during the 
first half. Our brand investments are translating into measurable outcomes. 
Against category growth of approximately 1.3%, our branded portfolio grew by 
nearly around nearly 8%, supporting 140 basis point increase in market share 
on year-to-date basis.  
Household reach increased from 56.2 lakhs to 67.5 lakhs over the last year. 
Through our project Vistaar, we are increasing direct distribution, feet-on-
street capabilities and assortment productivity. Alongside this, investments in 
supply chain and sales digitalization are improving forecasting, frontline 
execution and on-shelf availability.  
With branded basmati still significantly underpenetrated in India, we see a long 
runway to acquire consumers, premiumize the category and expand into 
adjacent consumption occasions. Now, I'll cover the United States. That United 
States remains our largest international market and an important growth 
engine supported by strong brands, category leadership and established 
omnichannel presence and strong distribution.  
We continue to strengthen our core rice portfolio while expanding into 
convenience-led and value-added consumption occasions. During the period, 
we advanced our ready-to-heat portfolio, expanding microwaveable formats 
and continued premiumization across Royal and Golden Star and rice.  
We are also investing in digital commerce and consumer discovery capabilities 
to keep our brands visible and relevant as the path to purchase increasingly 
moves across digital and AI-enabled platforms. Our ambition is to leverage our 
leadership into rice to build a broader branded foods platform in North 
America.

If I talk about Europe, Europe continues to be an important strategic market 
for us. While the operating environment remains challenging. We have made 
meaningful progress in strengthening the underlying business and creating a 
more scalable platform for the future growth. During the quarter, we further 
expanded our customer base and secured new mainstream private label 
business across Germany and the Nordic markets.  
We have strengthened our presence in France and are expanding our 
commercial coverage across Europe. Together, these initiatives are increasing

growth of 71% YoY 
Fractal Q2 Net Income Jumps 139% on revenue growth of 20% 
Mumbai | November 3, 2026: Fractal Analytics Ltd (BSE: 544700, NSE: FRACTAL), an enterprise AI 
company that builds its own AI models, platforms and products for Fortune 500® organizations, 
announced its consolidated ﬁnancial results for Q2 FY27, ending September 30, 2026.  
In Q2 FY27, the Company reported consolidated operating revenue of Rs 956.5 Cr, a growth of 20% 
year on year (YoY) and 10% in constant currency terms YoY. Revenue growth was led by the 
company’s Healthcare and Life Sciences (HLS) industry, which clocked 79% growth YoY. Banking, 
Financial Services and Insurance (BFSI) also performed very well, growing 30% YoY in Q2 and the 
company has delivered strong sustained growth in HLS and BFSI over the last several quarters. 
Fractal’s largest industry vertical, Consumer Packaged Goods and Retail (CPGR), grew 11% YoY. TMT 
saw strong sequential recovery with 6% QoQ growth. Fractal’s products, including the Cogentiq 
agentic AI platform, reached an annual revenue run-rate of over Rs 150 Cr, up 39% YoY. 
Fractal’s focus on deepening customer relationships continues to yield good outcomes. Its clients 
collectively increased their spending with the company, as reﬂected in the Net Revenue Retention1 
of 115% in Q2. Further, its Net Promoter Score (NPS) during the period stood at 76.  
The company reported improved proﬁt margins at all levels. Adjusted EBITDA Margin expanded by 
123 bps2 YoY to 16%. Net Income grew 139% YoY to Rs 79.2 Cr. 
Commenting on the performance, Srikanth Velamakanni, Co-founder and Group CEO said: 
“AI models are getting more capable every week and cheaper every quarter. Within the next few 
quarters, we will cross a threshold where it becomes irresponsible and downright risky for 
companies to leave their most important decisions unchanged. We are building Fractal for that 
moment, and this quarter shows it: revenue crossed $100 million and net income more than 
doubled.” 
About Fractal  
Fractal Analytics Ltd (BSE: 544700, NSE: FRACTAL) is an enterprise AI company with a vision to 
power every human decision in the enterprise. Fractal builds AI models, platforms and products, 
and engineers them into the critical decisions of Fortune 500® organizations. Fractal’s strategy is 
focused on three pillars: AIT, which rebuilds business workﬂows and decisions with AI; AIF, which 
builds the trusted, governed data and knowledge layer that enterprise AI reasons with; and AIW, 
which helps organizations redesign work, develop AI-ready talent, and build the capabilities 
needed for the AI-native enterprise. All three pillars are powered by Cogentiq, Fractal’s ﬂagship 
agentic AI platform.

Dear Sir/Madam, 
 
Pursuant to Regulation 30 & 33 read with Schedule III of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015, the Board of Directors of the Company at its meeting held today i.e. 
November 3, 2026 have inter-alia approved and taken on record the following: 
 
1. The Un-audited Financial Results (Standalone and Consolidated) of the Company for the 
quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026 along with Limited review report issued by 
M/s SCV & Co. LLP, Chartered Accountants, Statutory Auditors of the Company is enclosed as 
Annexure-l. 
 
2. Formulation, adaption and implementation of the "HEG Advanced Materials Limited 
Employee Stock Option Plan 2026" for grant of Employee Stock options to the eligible 
employees of the Company and its subsidiaries under this plan, subject to the approval of 
shareholders and other regulatory authorities as may be applicable as per the provisions of 
the SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefit & Sweat Equity Shares) Regulations, 2021. The 
detailed disclosure is enclosed as Annexure – II. 
 
3. Based on the recommendation of the Nomination & Remuneration Committee, Shri Hiren 
Pravin Shah, Managing Director & CEO of Replus Engitech Private Limited, a subsidiary 
company and Shri Ankur Khaitan, Managing Director & CEO of TACC Limited, a wholly owned 
subsidiary company, have been designated as Senior Management Personnel. The detailed

Sub: Outcome of Board Meeting held on November 3, 2026 
 
Dear Sir/Madam, 
 
Pursuant to Regulation 30 & 33 read with Schedule III of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015, the Board of Directors of the Company at its meeting held today i.e. 
November 3, 2026 have inter-alia approved and taken on record the following: 
 
1. The Un-audited Financial Results (Standalone and Consolidated) of the Company for the 
quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026 along with Limited review report issued by 
M/s SCV & Co. LLP, Chartered Accountants, Statutory Auditors of the Company is enclosed as 
Annexure-l. 
 
2. Formulation, adaption and implementation of the "HEG Advanced Materials Limited 
Employee Stock Option Plan 2026" for grant of Employee Stock options to the eligible 
employees of the Company and its subsidiaries under this plan, subject to the approval of 
shareholders and other regulatory authorities as may be applicable as per the provisions of 
the SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefit & Sweat Equity Shares) Regulations, 2021. The 
detailed disclosure is enclosed as Annexure – II. 
 
3. Based on the recommendation of the Nomination & Remuneration Committee, Shri Hiren 
Pravin Shah, Managing Director & CEO of Replus Engitech Private Limited, a subsidiary 
company and Shri Ankur Khaitan, Managing Director & CEO of TACC Limited, a wholly owned 
subsidiary company, have been designated as Senior Management Personnel. The detailed 
disclosure is enclosed as Annexure – III.  
 
4. Closure of LNJ Trading FZCO, a foreign wholly owned subsidiary of the Company situated in 
Dubai. The closure is being undertaken pursuant to a rationalization of the Group's overseas 
corporate structure. The Group's business interests and future opportunities in the 
jurisdiction will continue to be pursued through another subsidiary, enabling greater 
operational and administrative efficiency. The detailed disclosure is enclosed as Annexure – 
IV. 
 
5. Cessation of M/s. S.L. Chhajed & Co. Chartered Accountants, Internal Auditor: The detailed 
disclosure is enclosed as Annexure – V 
 

 
 
6. Based on the recommendation of Audit Committee, appointment of M/s BGJC & Associates 
LLP, Chartered Accountants (FRN.003304N/N500056) as an Internal Auditor of the Company 
for the Financial Year 2026-27. The detailed disclosure is enclosed as Annexure – V  
 
7. Alteration of the main object clause of Memorandum of Association (MOA) of the company 
by inserting the objects relating to Anode, Graphene, crucible, advanced carbon materials and 
other allied material, subject to the approval of shareholders.  
 
8. Approval for grant of additional loan of Rs. 50 crore (revolving) to Replus Engitech Private 
Limited, a subsidiary of the Company. The detailed disclosure is enclosed as Annexure – VI 
 
9. Approval relating to TACC Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary company. 
 
The Board of Directors of the Company have approved the following:  
 
a) Revised cost of completion of Phase-1 of 20,000 MT Anode project. The estimated revised 
cost is ~ Rs. 2,350 crore for Phase-1 capacity of 20,000 MT with target COD by June 27 of 
the anode project. 
 
b) Proposal for expansion plan by increasing the capacity from 20,000 MT to 44,000 MT. The 
estimated cost is ~ Rs. 1606 crore with target COD by March 2029. The detailed disclosure 
is enclosed as Annexure – VII 
 
c) Setting up of new plant to manufacture Crucible with capacity of 80,000 units P.A. The 
estimated cost is ~ Rs. 475 crore with target COD by September 2028. The detailed 
disclosure is enclosed as Annexure – VIII  
 
10. Approval relating to HEG Graphene Materials Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary company. 
 
a) Setting up of manufacturing plant of 500 MT Graphene in two phases at an estimated cost 
of ~ Rs. 500 crore with target COD by September 2028. The detailed disclosure is enclosed 
as Annexure – XI  
 
 

 
 
Disclosure under Regulation 30 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulation, 
2015 read with SEBI Master Circular No. HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFD-POD2/I/3762/2026 dated January 
30, 2026 are enclosed as annexures. 
 
The Board Meeting commenced at 02:30 P.M. and concluded at 08:30 P.M. 
 
Please take the above information on record. 
 
Yours truly, 
For HEG Advanced Materials Limited 
(formerly HEG Limited)

1. 
We have reviewed the accompanying Statement of Unaudited Standalone Financial Results of HEG 
Advanced Materials Limited (formerly known as HEG Limited) (hereinafter referred to as “the 
Company"), for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026 ("the Statement"), being submitted 
pursuant to the requirement of Regulation 33 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015, as amended (“the Listing Regulations”). 
2. 
This Statement, which is the responsibility of the Company's Management and approved by the 
Company's Board of Directors, has been prepared in accordance with the recognition and measurement 
principles laid down in the Indian Accounting Standard 34 "Interim Financial Reporting" ("Ind AS 34"), 
prescribed under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013, read with relevant rules issued thereunder and 
other accounting principles generally accepted in India and in compliance with the listing regulations. Our 
responsibility is to express a conclusion on the Statement based on our review. 
3. 
We conducted our review of the Statement in accordance with the Standard on Review Engagements 
(SRE) 2410, “Review of Interim Financial Information Performed by the Independent Auditor 
of the Entity”, 
issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India. This standard requires that we plan and perform 
the review to obtain moderate assurance as to whether the Statement is free of material misstatement. A 
review of interim financial information consists of making inquiries, primarily of persons responsible for 
financial and accounting matters, and applying analytical and other review procedures. A review is 
substantially less in scope than an audit conducted in accordance with Standards on Auditing and 
consequently does not enable us to obtain assurance that we would become aware of all significant 
matters that might be identified in an audit. Accordingly, we do not express an audit opinion. 
4. 
Based on our review conducted as stated in paragraph 3 above, nothing has come to our attention that 
causes us to believe that the accompanying Statement, prepared in accordance with the recognition and 
measurement principles laid down in the applicable Indian Accounting Standards ('Ind AS') specified 
under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013, read with relevant rules issued thereunder and other 
accounting principles generally accepted in India, has not disclosed the information required to be 
disclosed in terms of Listing Regulations , including the manner in which it is to be disclosed, or that it 
contains any material misstatement.

Emphasis of Matter 
5. We draw attention to Note 3 to the Statement regarding the Composite Scheme of Arrangement 
between HEG Advanced Materials Limited (formerly “HEG Limited”) (the “Company or “Demerged 
Company”), HEG Limited (formerly “HEG Graphite Limited”) (“Resulting Company”) and Bhilwara Energy 
Limited (“Transferor Company”) and their respective shareholders and creditors under Sections 230 to 232 
read with other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 (“Scheme”), inter alia, providing for-the 
demerger of the Graphite Undertaking including overseas investment and assets and liabilities pertaining 
to TAWA power plant of the Company into the Resulting Company and amalgamation of the Transferor 
Company with the Company . The Merger of Bhilwara Energy Limited has been given effect to in the 
Statement in accordance with “Appendix C - Business Combination of entities under common control” to 
Ind AS 103 “Business Combinations”, as prescribed in the Scheme. w.e.f appointed date (i.e April 1, 2024) 
.The financial results of corresponding quarter June 30, 2026 , September 30, 2025 and half year ended 
September 30, 2025 year ended March 31, 2026 has been restated to give effect to the merger . Financial 
results/statement of the Bhilwara Energy Limited (Transferor company) has been reviewed and audited 
respectively by another auditor whose reports dated July 21, 2026, November 7, 2025 and April 27, 2026 
respectively, expressed unmodified conclusion/opinion on those results. The demerger has been 
accounted) forin the current quarter in accordance with the accounting treatment specified in the Scheme 
w.e.f the effective date (i.e September 1, 2026) and operations of the Graphite undertaking including 
overseas investment and assets and liabilities pertaining 
to TAWA power plant of the comparative period(s) 
have been classified as "Discontinued operations" in accordance with Ind AS 105 "Non-current Assets Held 
for Sale and Discontinued Operations”. 
Our Conclusion is not modified in respect to this matter.

Q2 FY27 
 
● Board approves expansion of current 20,000 MT capacity anode plant to 44,000 MT 
at a capex of INR 1606 Cr ( 20,000 MT to come into operation by Jun 2027 and 
balance 24,000 MT by March 2029 ) 
 
● Board approves crucible project to have backward integration and cost optimisation 
with the anode plant , with a capex of INR 475 Cr 
 
● Board approves graphene project of 500 MTPA at a capex of INR 500 Cr 
 
● ESOP scheme implemented 
 
 
Noida, 3 November 2026: HEG Advanced Materials Limited (NSE: HEGAM | BSE: 509631), part 
of the LNJ Bhilwara Group, today announced its financial results for the quarter and half year 
ended 30 September 2026. 
For H1 FY27, consolidated revenue from continuing operations stood at ₹725.80 crore and total 
income at ₹870.77 crore, with EBITDA of ₹438.00 crore and profit after tax of ₹269.07 crore. As 
on 30 September 2026, consolidated cash and bank balances stood at ₹1322.84 crore. 
For Q2 FY27, the Company reported consolidated revenue from continuing operations of ₹429.94 
crore, total income of ₹546.59 crore, EBITDA of ₹312.78 crore and profit after tax of ₹208.89 
crore. 
Mr. Riju Jhunjhunwala, Chairman, MD & CEO, HEG Advanced Materials Limited, said, “Q2 FY27 
reflects our continued progress towards building HEG Advanced Materials into a technology-led, 
globally competitive advanced materials platform. Our focus is on strengthening R&D, 
developing proprietary technologies and creating differentiated, scalable businesses across 
anode materials, graphene, battery energy storage and green power. Our motto remains - 
research to revenue! As we move forward, our priorities remain disciplined capital allocation,  

 
 
 
 
timely execution, customer development and improving the long-term competitiveness of each 
business. We believe these initiatives will strengthen our growth potential, create multiple 
avenues for value creation and deliver sustainable returns for our shareholders over the long 
term” 
Ms. Neha Rajvanshi, President & CFO, HEG Advanced Materials Limited, said, “Q2 and H1 FY27 
performance reflects the evolving business mix and varying stages of development across our 
verticals, while our underlying fundamentals remain stable. Our Green Power Business, with its 
differentiated model, profitable operations, debt-free position and stable cash flows, provides 
a sound financial foundation for the Group. REPLUS is strengthening its presence in Battery 
Energy Storage Systems (BESS) and EV solutions, enabling the Group to participate in the 
evolving energy transition. We are particularly excited about the upcoming anode expansion,  
graphene and crucible projects, which will further strengthen our product portfolio and 
reinforce our position in the advanced materials industry. Our focus remains on building HEG 
Advanced Materials into a globally competitive company, diversifying revenues and creating 
sustainable value.” 
Business highlights 
● Advanced Materials (TACC): Global lithium-ion battery production is expected to grow from 
about 2.3 TWh in 2025 to about 8 TWh by 2035, with non-China anode demand set to exceed 
1 
Mn 
tons 
by 
2030 
as 
cell 
makers 
diversify 
their 
supply 
chains.  
 
To serve this demand, construction of the Phase I 20,000 MT anode materials facility has 
reached 61% overall progress, with the process building at 72.25 COD planned for June 2027.  
Phase II, an additional 24,000 MT plant targeting COD in March 2029 on the existing 
infrastructure, power connection and land at the Dewas site, will take total anode capacity 
to 44,000 MT. TACC's R&D pipeline includes next-generation silicon-doped and graphene-
based anodes for higher energy density and faster charging. TACC received the CII Award 
for Excellence in R&D 2026 in the Materials, Chemicals & Textiles - Large Enterprise category 
in October 2026. 
Battery Energy Solutions (REPLUS Engitech): REPLUS has deployed over 1 GWh of energy 
storage capacity across BESS, electric mobility, telecom power solutions and hybrid  

 
 
 
 
energy applications. Alongside its operational 1 GWh Giga Factory in Pune, a 5 GWh high-
speed, fully automatic prismatic line expansion facility is under construction, which will 
take total manufacturing capacity to 6 GWh on completion. 
 
● Green Power Businesses: The Green Power Businesses have a combined hydroelectric 
installed capacity of 278 MW in Himachal Pradesh, through the 86 MW Malana Power 
Company Limited project (MPCL) and the 192 MW AD Hydro Power Limited project, along 
with a 14 MW wind power project in Maharashtra (under HEGAM). Both operating hydro 
projects and the wind project are debt-free, and the existing hydro assets generate annually 
stable cash flows of over ₹300 crore. The 200 MWh BESS IPP in Gujarat for Gujarat Urja Vikas 
Nigam Limited, with a total capex of ₹227.8 crore, has reached 64% project progress and 
targets commissioning in Q3 FY27. 
The HEG Composite Scheme became effective on 1 September 2026. Under the Scheme, the 
graphite electrodes business was transferred to HEG Limited (earlier known as HEG Graphite 
Limited), and Bhilwara Energy Limited was amalgamated into the Company. The results 
accordingly present continuing and discontinued operations separately. Current financial figures 
are not comparable to previous financial figures owing to demerger of HEG Limited. 
About HEG Advanced Materials Limited 
HEG Advanced Materials Ltd., part of the LNJ Bhilwara Group is a new-age platform spanning 
advanced battery materials with a strong manufacturing, R&D, and innovation foundation, and 
also into the business of battery energy solutions & green power. Compounding on HEG’s 50+ 
years of expertise in graphitization and manufacturing know-how, the platform is developing a 
large-scale anode materials business and future material development, including silicon-based 
anodes. Its capabilities span research to revenue, from advanced research and product 
development to commercialization, serving the evolving EV, BESS, and energy-storage 
ecosystem.

capacity expansions and timelines, capital expenditure plans, market and demand projections  

 
 
 
 
and order pipelines. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and 
are subject to known and unknown risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially 
from those expressed or implied. The Company undertakes no obligation to publicly update or

● Company reports consolidated revenue of ₹429.94 crore, EBITDA of ₹312.78 crore in 
Q2 FY27 
 
● Board approves expansion of current 20,000 MT capacity anode plant to 44,000 MT 
at a capex of INR 1606 Cr ( 20,000 MT to come into operation by Jun 2027 and 
balance 24,000 MT by March 2029 ) 
 
● Board approves crucible project to have backward integration and cost optimisation 
with the anode plant , with a capex of INR 475 Cr 
 
● Board approves graphene project of 500 MTPA at a capex of INR 500 Cr

Noida, 3 November 2026: HEG Advanced Materials Limited (NSE: HEGAM | BSE: 509631), part 
of the LNJ Bhilwara Group, today announced its financial results for the quarter and half year 
ended 30 September 2026. 
For H1 FY27, consolidated revenue from continuing operations stood at ₹725.80 crore and total 
income at ₹870.77 crore, with EBITDA of ₹438.00 crore and profit after tax of ₹269.07 crore. As 
on 30 September 2026, consolidated cash and bank balances stood at ₹1322.84 crore. 
For Q2 FY27, the Company reported consolidated revenue from continuing operations of ₹429.94 
crore, total income of ₹546.59 crore, EBITDA of ₹312.78 crore and profit after tax of ₹208.89 
crore. 
Mr. Riju Jhunjhunwala, Chairman, MD & CEO, HEG Advanced Materials Limited, said, “Q2 FY27 
reflects our continued progress towards building HEG Advanced Materials into a technology-led, 
globally competitive advanced materials platform. Our focus is on strengthening R&D, 
developing proprietary technologies and creating differentiated, scalable businesses across 
anode materials, graphene, battery energy storage and green power. Our motto remains - 
research to revenue! As we move forward, our priorities remain disciplined capital allocation,  

 
 
 
 
timely execution, customer development and improving the long-term competitiveness of each 
business. We believe these initiatives will strengthen our growth potential, create multiple 
avenues for value creation and deliver sustainable returns for our shareholders over the long 
term” 
Ms. Neha Rajvanshi, President & CFO, HEG Advanced Materials Limited, said, “Q2 and H1 FY27 
performance reflects the evolving business mix and varying stages of development across our 
verticals, while our underlying fundamentals remain stable. Our Green Power Business, with its 
differentiated model, profitable operations, debt-free position and stable cash flows, provides 
a sound financial foundation for the Group. REPLUS is strengthening its presence in Battery 
Energy Storage Systems (BESS) and EV solutions, enabling the Group to participate in the 
evolving energy transition. We are particularly excited about the upcoming anode expansion,  
graphene and crucible projects, which will further strengthen our product portfolio and 
reinforce our position in the advanced materials industry. Our focus remains on building HEG 
Advanced Materials into a globally competitive company, diversifying revenues and creating 
sustainable value.” 
Business highlights 
● Advanced Materials (TACC): Global lithium-ion battery production is expected to grow from 
about 2.3 TWh in 2025 to about 8 TWh by 2035, with non-China anode demand set to exceed 
1 
Mn 
tons 
by 
2030 
as 
cell 
makers 
diversify 
their 
supply 
chains.  
 
To serve this demand, construction of the Phase I 20,000 MT anode materials facility has 
reached 61% overall progress, with the process building at 72.25 COD planned for June 2027.  
Phase II, an additional 24,000 MT plant targeting COD in March 2029 on the existing 
infrastructure, power connection and land at the Dewas site, will take total anode capacity 
to 44,000 MT. TACC's R&D pipeline includes next-generation silicon-doped and graphene-
based anodes for higher energy density and faster charging. TACC received the CII Award 
for Excellence in R&D 2026 in the Materials, Chemicals & Textiles - Large Enterprise category 
in October 2026. 
Battery Energy Solutions (REPLUS Engitech): REPLUS has deployed over 1 GWh of energy 
storage capacity across BESS, electric mobility, telecom power solutions and hybrid  

 
 
 
 
energy applications. Alongside its operational 1 GWh Giga Factory in Pune, a 5 GWh high-
speed, fully automatic prismatic line expansion facility is under construction, which will 
take total manufacturing capacity to 6 GWh on completion. 
 
● Green Power Businesses: The Green Power Businesses have a combined hydroelectric 
installed capacity of 278 MW in Himachal Pradesh, through the 86 MW Malana Power 
Company Limited project (MPCL) and the 192 MW AD Hydro Power Limited project, along 
with a 14 MW wind power project in Maharashtra (under HEGAM). Both operating hydro 
projects and the wind project are debt-free, and the existing hydro assets generate annually 
stable cash flows of over ₹300 crore. The 200 MWh BESS IPP in Gujarat for Gujarat Urja Vikas 
Nigam Limited, with a total capex of ₹227.8 crore, has reached 64% project progress and 
targets commissioning in Q3 FY27. 
The HEG Composite Scheme became effective on 1 September 2026. Under the Scheme, the 
graphite electrodes business was transferred to HEG Limited (earlier known as HEG Graphite 
Limited), and Bhilwara Energy Limited was amalgamated into the Company. The results 
accordingly present continuing and discontinued operations separately. Current financial figures 
are not comparable to previous financial figures owing to demerger of HEG Limited. 
About HEG Advanced Materials Limited 
HEG Advanced Materials Ltd., part of the LNJ Bhilwara Group is a new-age platform spanning 
advanced battery materials with a strong manufacturing, R&D, and innovation foundation, and 
also into the business of battery energy solutions & green power. Compounding on HEG’s 50+ 
years of expertise in graphitization and manufacturing know-how, the platform is developing a 
large-scale anode materials business and future material development, including silicon-based 
anodes. Its capabilities span research to revenue, from advanced research and product 
development to commercialization, serving the evolving EV, BESS, and energy-storage 
ecosystem.
